modules.title: Module 1 — What occupational safety is and why it matters
modules.summary: This module sets the foundation for the whole day. You will learn what occupational safety and health means, how harm happens at work, and why Namibian employers and workers each carry legal duties. The aim is practical: by the end you should be able to recognise unsafe conditions and unsafe acts as separate problems, and know that both are reportable.
points: Define occupational safety and health, hazard, risk, incident and near miss.
Describe, in plain language, why workplace safety is a legal duty in Namibia and not only a company preference.
Distinguish between unsafe conditions and unsafe acts, and give one example of each from your own work area.
Explain the direct and indirect costs of a workplace incident to a worker, a family and a business.
State who enforces occupational safety law in Namibia and what an inspector can do.
Occupational safety and health (OSH) — The field concerned with preventing injury and illness arising from work.

modules.title: Module 2 — Legal duties of employers and employees
modules.summary: This module turns the law into a working tool. You will separate what the employer must do from what you as a worker must do, learn what happens after a workplace injury is reported, and see where the pending OSH Bill may take Namibian workplaces. The goal is that you can answer, without guessing, who is responsible for what.
points: List the employer's core safety duties under the Labour Act, 2007.
List the employee's core safety duties under the same Act.
Describe the reporting chain after a workplace injury, including the Employees' Compensation claim.
Explain the difference between a safety instruction you may question and one you must follow.
State two changes the pending OSH Bill is expected to introduce, and note that it is not yet law.
Duty of care — The employer's obligation to protect employee health, safety and welfare so far as is reasonably practicable.

modules.title: Module 3 — Hazard identification and reporting
modules.summary: This is the core skill of the whole induction. You will learn a simple method for finding hazards before they find you, practise it against realistic workplace descriptions, and write a report that a supervisor can act on. Everything in the later modules builds on this one.
points: Sort hazards into the six standard categories.
Apply the Stop, Look, Assess, Manage (SLAM) routine before starting a task.
Write a factual hazard or near-miss report that names the location, the hazard, the people exposed and the suggested fix.
State to whom a hazard report goes and what should happen next.
SLAM — Stop, Look, Assess, Manage: a routine for checking a task before and during the work.
Hierarchy of reporting — The agreed route a hazard report travels, normally supervisor, then safety representative, then safety officer or management.

modules.title: Module 4 — Personal protective equipment: what, when, how
modules.summary: Personal protective equipment is the last line of defence, not the first solution. This module places PPE in its correct position in the hierarchy of control, then covers selection, inspection, care and the limits of each common item. The Namibian climate adds its own demands: sun, heat and dust.
points: Place PPE correctly in the hierarchy of control and explain why it sits last.
Match common PPE items to the hazards they address.
Inspect a hard hat, a pair of safety boots and a hi-vis vest for serviceability before use.
Describe heat and sun risks in Namibian outdoor work and the controls that address them.
Hierarchy of control — The ranked order of controls: elimination, substitution, engineering controls, administrative controls, and only then personal protective equipment.
Engineering control — A physical change to the workplace or equipment that removes the hazard, such as a guard or local exhaust ventilation.

modules.title: Module 5 — Emergency procedures
modules.summary: Emergencies compress every safety decision into seconds. This module makes the decisions in advance: what counts as an emergency, what the alarm sounds like, where the exits and assembly point are, who does what, and what never to do. Fire response is covered at awareness level; practical extinguisher use belongs to Level 2 and to qualified providers.
points: List the classes of emergency a Namibian workplace should plan for.
State your own workplace's alarm signal, evacuation routes and assembly point.
Describe the correct response on hearing the alarm, including the no-re-entry rule.
Match the basic fire classes with the extinguishing media that suit them, at awareness level.
Report an injury or emergency correctly, including who calls whom.
Assembly point — A pre-agreed safe location where everyone gathers to be counted after evacuation.

modules.title: Module 6 — Manual handling and basic ergonomics
modules.summary: More working days are lost to backs, shoulders and wrists than to dramatic events. This module covers the TILE assessment, the lifting technique that protects the spine, when to refuse and get help, and the small adjustments that make office work less damaging. It closes the induction content.
points: Assess a manual-handling task using TILE: task, individual, load, environment.
Demonstrate the safe lifting technique for a moderate load.
State the sensible cut-off for a one-person lift and the alternatives available.
Adjust a computer workstation using a short checklist, and explain the purpose of breaks and task rotation.
Manual handling — Any transporting or supporting of a load by human effort: lifting, lowering, pushing, pulling, carrying.
TILE — Task, Individual, Load, Environment: the four factors assessed before handling.

bank.q: Which law places the main duty on Namibian employers to protect employees at work?
A scaffold plank falls past a worker and hits nobody. This is best described as…
options: A near miss that should be reported

bank.q: Which ministry's inspectors enforce occupational safety in Namibian workplaces?
options: Ministry of Health and Social Services
Ministry of Labour, Industrial Relations and Employment Creation

bank.q: Who pays for personal protective equipment required under the law?
Reporting a near miss is…
options: A legal duty of the employee

bank.q: The OSH Bill of 2024 is currently…
Where does a hazard report go first in the standard route?
Which control is wet cutting of concrete blocks, instead of dry cutting with a dust mask?
A hard hat receives a significant impact but shows no crack. What should happen?
options: Continue use, it did its job

bank.q: You are at the assembly point and remember your phone at your desk. The alarm is still sounding. What do you do?
options: Stay out and report to roll call
Ask a colleague to fetch it

bank.q: Which extinguishing media are suitable for a flammable-liquid fire?
options: Foam, dry powder or carbon dioxide

bank.q: Which muscles should do the work in a correct lift?
A task needs a 40-kilogram bag moved twenty metres. What is the correct decision?
options: One-person lift with a straight back

modules.title: Module 1 — The Namibian occupational safety framework in depth
modules.summary: Level 1 taught the duties. This module maps the whole framework a safety representative works inside: the Act, the regulations, the compensation system, the inspectorate, and the industry standards used as good practice even where they are not Namibian law. The goal is a working reference you can quote accurately in a meeting.
points: Summarise the structure of Namibian occupational safety law: the Labour Act, 2007, GN 156 of 1997, and the pending OSH Bill.
Explain what a labour inspector may lawfully do on a site visit, and what records they may ask to see.
Distinguish clearly between Namibian statute, international standards, and South African standards used as good practice.
Describe the employees' compensation system and the reporting chain after a workplace injury.
Locate the primary sources, so claims can be checked rather than remembered.
Statutory instrument — Law made under an Act, such as a regulation or government notice.

modules.title: Module 2 — Hazard identification and risk assessment (HIRA)
modules.summary: HIRA is the working heart of the safety officer's job. This module teaches the full cycle: identifying hazards systematically, scoring risk on a matrix, choosing controls in the correct order, documenting the assessment so others can use it, and reviewing it when things change. You will produce a real risk assessment during the course and be assessed on one.
points: Run a structured hazard identification across a work area, using task-based and area-based sweeps.
Score risks on a five-by-five likelihood-severity matrix and explain the score to a supervisor.
Select controls using the hierarchy of control, in writing, with reasons.
Document a risk assessment that a third party can follow, and state the triggers that force its review.
Present risk information to workers in a form they can act on.
HIRA — Hazard identification and risk assessment: the structured cycle of finding hazards and judging risk.

modules.title: Module 3 — Incident investigation and reporting
modules.summary: When something goes wrong, the safety officer becomes the company's memory. This module covers the first hour after an incident, evidence handling, a structured cause method that reaches system faults rather than blaming the nearest worker, and the written report. It also covers the near-miss programme that prevents the investigation ever being needed.
points: Manage the first response to an incident: treatment, scene control, notification.
Preserve evidence, physical, documentary and human, to a defensible standard.
Investigate causes with the five-whys method extended to system level.
Write an incident report with findings, causes and corrective actions that closes the loop.
Operate a near-miss reporting routine that workers actually use.
Immediate cause — The direct act or condition in the final seconds before the incident.

modules.title: Module 4 — PPE inspection and management
modules.summary: Level 1 covered wearing PPE. This module covers running a PPE programme: selecting correctly against a hazard, issuing with records, inspecting on a schedule, storing, replacing, and retiring. A managed programme is auditable; a box of gloves is not.
points: Build a PPE matrix linking each role's hazards to specified equipment, including standards markings.
Set up issue and inspection records that survive an audit.
Inspect and correctly retire common items, hard hats, harnesses, respirators, gloves, boots.
Manage storage and hygiene for shared and personal equipment.
Recognise the markings that indicate protection level, including EN and equivalent standards, and what they do not mean.
PPE matrix — A table linking roles, hazards, specified PPE, and standards or specifications.

modules.title: Module 5 — Emergency preparedness and fire safety
modules.summary: This module plans emergencies rather than surviving them: the written plan, the evacuation diagram, the drill cycle, and fire science at officer level, fuel classes, spread mechanisms, extinguishing media, and equipment maintenance. Practical extinguisher use is scheduled as a live session delivered through a qualified fire-training provider; this classroom module prepares you to pass it and to own the site's arrangements afterwards.
points: Draft the core of a site emergency plan: roles, alarm, routes, assembly, and communications.
Read and brief an evacuation diagram, including for visitors and people with limited mobility.
Run a drill cycle with objectives, observation and a written debrief.
Classify fires by fuel and specify the correct medium and the media that must not be used.
Set up and record monthly and annual fire-equipment checks with competent servicing.
Emergency plan — The written arrangement answering: alarm, routes, assembly, roles, communications.

modules.title: Module 6 — First aid awareness
modules.summary: This module is deliberately named awareness. It equips the safety officer to arrange and manage first aid, not to substitute for a first aider. Certification in First Aid Level 1 or higher is issued through a registered Namibian first-aid training partner under a separate programme; this module explains what that arrangement is, what a compliant site looks like, and the correct first response while waiting for qualified help.
points: State what first aid is and what it is not, including the certification boundary on Oryx courses.
Determine first-aid provision expectations for a workplace under GN 156 of 1997, including boxes, contents and trained cover per shift.
Manage the first response to bleeding, burns, fractures and unconsciousness while awaiting trained help.
Check and restock a first-aid box on a schedule, with records.
Brief a partner-delivered First Aid Level 1 course and integrate certificates into the training register.
First aider — A person trained and certified to provide initial treatment; on Oryx-linked sites, certified by a registered Namibian first-aid training partner.

modules.title: Module 7 — Construction-site safety
modules.summary: Construction concentrates nearly every hazard category into one moving site. This module covers the high-risk subjects a safety officer must know cold, scaffolds, work at height, excavations, electricity and mobile plant, framed within Namibian law and honest about which standards are good practice. The recurring theme is the same one auditors use: is the safe method written, resourced and checked, or improvised?
points: List the high-risk construction activities that need a written, controlled method before work starts.
Inspect a scaffold systematically against a checklist and state common faults that stop work.
Specify the protective measures for excavations, edges, openings and fragile surfaces.
Describe the electrical safety arrangements a non-electrician officer verifies: isolation, protection, inspection of leads and tools.
Manage mobile plant and pedestrian separation, including delivery and reversing operations.
Working at height — Any work where a fall could cause injury, including below-ground work near openings; there is no two-metre exemption in logic, whatever local myth says.

modules.title: Module 8 — Toolbox talks and safety meetings
modules.summary: A safety officer who cannot talk to a crew is a filing clerk. This module builds the two speaking formats of the job: the five-minute toolbox talk that changes tomorrow's behaviour, and the safety meeting that moves the site's system. Both are assessable: your ten-minute toolbox talk is part of the final assessment.
points: Plan and deliver a five-minute toolbox talk on one hazard, to a standard rubric.
Select topics from the site's live risk information rather than a generic list.
Chair a safety meeting with an agenda, minutes, and actions that carry owners and dates.
Handle resistance and silence in a way that keeps reports coming.
Toolbox talk — A short, single-topic safety briefing at the workface, ideally delivered with the crew standing where the hazard is.
Safety meeting — A scheduled, minuted meeting of site management and worker representatives on safety matters.

modules.title: Module 9 — Safety files and site documentation
modules.summary: The safety file is where the site's safety system becomes visible and checkable. This module assembles one: what belongs inside, how documents are controlled so the current version is the one on the wall, and how the permit-to-work discipline governs the highest-risk tasks. An auditor should be able to reconstruct your site's whole safety story from the file, and so should your successor.
points: List the contents of a complete site safety file and assemble one from a checklist.
Control document versions so superseded copies leave the wall and the site.
Explain permit-to-work logic and operate a basic permit for hot work or work at height.
Maintain the registers, training, inspection, incident, PPE, plant, as living records rather than archived paper.
Hand over a safety file that a successor or auditor can navigate in ten minutes.
Safety file — The controlled collection of a site's safety documents and registers, current, complete and indexed.

modules.title: Module 10 — The practical site walkthrough
modules.summary: The walkthrough is where the course stops being knowledge and becomes performance. You will inspect a real or simulated site with a checklist, classify findings, decide what to stop and what to monitor, communicate to the crew, and write the inspection report. It is assessed by observation against a published rubric, and it rehearses the routine you will run weekly for the rest of your career.
points: Plan a walkthrough: route, documents carried, who accompanies, what yesterday's records say.
Inspect systematically, using the area and task sweep patterns from Module 2.
Classify findings as stop-work, fix-with-date, or monitor, and justify each classification.
Communicate findings on site, to the crew and the supervisor, without blame and without vagueness.
Write the follow-up report with actions, owners and dates, and file it in the safety file.
Finding — A specific observed condition or behaviour, stated with location and evidence.

bank.q: The OSH Bill 2024 is currently…
On the course 5x5 matrix, a hazard scores 3x5=15. What does convention require?
In a serious-injury case, who controls the scene?
options: The police and labour inspectorate once involved; nothing moves until released

bank.q: The five-whys method stops when…
options: The chain reaches a management system fault
Five questions have been asked regardless

bank.q: Where does a PPE programme start?
A harness has arrested one fall and shows no damage. What happens?
Which medium suits a live electrical fire in an enclosed switch room?
Does this Oryx course certify you in first aid?
options: No; certification runs through a registered Namibian first-aid training partner
Yes, if you pass the exam

bank.q: Cool a burn with…
options: Cool water for a sustained period

bank.q: A soaked dressing on a bleeding wound should be…
Is there a dedicated Namibian construction safety regulation equivalent to South Africa's Construction Regulations 2014?
options: No; the Labour Act and GN 156 apply, with SA instruments used as contractual good practice

modules.title: Module 1 — SHEQ management systems and ISO 45001 principles
modules.summary: This module builds the management-system view of safety: policy, planning, support, operation, evaluation and improvement wired together so the system, not heroics, produces performance. ISO 45001:2018 provides the reference architecture; the module teaches its logic, not certification consultancy, and how to run a gap analysis against it.
points: Explain the PDCA cycle and map the ISO 45001:2018 clause structure onto it.
Describe what each major clause family demands, context, leadership, planning, support, operation, evaluation, improvement.
Identify the legal-and-other-requirements inputs a Namibian organisation must feed the system, and how to keep them current.
Conduct a structured gap analysis of an organisation against ISO 45001 principles and prioritise the gaps.
Design the documentation architecture that serves the system without burying it.
SHEQ — Safety, health, environment and quality managed as one integrated system.

modules.title: Module 2 — Construction safety requirements in depth
modules.summary: Beyond the Level 2 foundation, this module treats construction as a managed production system: design-stage risk reduction, method statements, temporary works, lifting operations, occupation and handover. The Namibian legal frame remains the Labour Act and GN 156; South African instruments appear as contractual good practice, labelled honestly.
points: Apply prevention-through-design thinking to a construction programme.
Specify the contents and discipline of method statements for high-risk activities.
Manage temporary works, scaffolds, formwork and excavation support, as engineered items with checks.
Plan lifting operations: equipment certification, lift categories, exclusion and supervision.
Run a construction-phase safety programme: inductions, inspections, permits, coordination and handover.
Method statement — A written, task-specific safe system of work: sequence, hazards, controls, competencies, checks.

modules.title: Module 3 — Mining safety requirements
modules.summary: Mining concentrates hazards at industrial scale: ground, mobile equipment, energy, dust and isolation. This module teaches transferable mine-site safety management while being scrupulously honest about the legal position: Namibia's mining industry operates under the Minerals (Prospecting and Mining) Act, 1992, administered by the Ministry of Mines and Energy, with mine safety requirements applied through that framework, while many operations use the South African Mine Health and Safety Act as the regional...
points: Describe the Namibian regulatory position for mining, including what must be verified before citation.
Manage the classic mine hazard families: ground control, mobile equipment interaction, energy isolation, dust and ventilation basics.
Structure the elements of a mine safety programme: risk assessment, codes of practice, training, and health surveillance.
Explain why codes of practice and shift-start meetings dominate mine safety communication.
Code of practice (mine) — A site-specific documented procedure for managing a identified major hazard, a regional mining convention.
Ground control — The management of rock mass stability, support and seismics in underground and open-pit operations.

modules.title: Module 4 — Occupational hygiene and environmental monitoring
modules.summary: Occupational hygiene is the science of measuring what you cannot see: dust, noise, heat, vapours and fumes at concentrations that injure slowly. This module teaches anticipation, recognition, evaluation and control of health hazards, survey design, the meaning of exposure limits, and how to commission and read monitoring reports without pretending to be a hygienist.
points: Run the hygiene cycle: anticipate, recognise, evaluate, control, re-verify.
Design a basic exposure survey: who, where, when, how long, what method.
Interpret exposure results against occupational exposure limits, including the statistical treatment of shift exposure.
Apply the control hierarchy to health hazards, with ventilation and process change leading.
Commission specialist monitoring competently and audit the report's quality.
Occupational exposure limit (OEL) — An airborne concentration ceiling used to judge exposure acceptability; source-dependent and jurisdiction-dependent.

modules.title: Module 5 — Contractor management
modules.summary: Most major incidents on client sites involve contractors, not employees. This module builds the contractor lifecycle: prequalification, contract terms, induction, supervision, permits and performance review, with the client's duty to coordinate rather than delegate away. The pervasive failure is treating contractors as someone else's problem; the module's thesis is the opposite.
points: Structure a contractor lifecycle from prequalification to post-contract review.
Write safety terms into contracts that are enforceable and auditable.
Design an induction that transfers the site's real risks, not a video.
Supervise contractor work: verification versus inspection, and the permit interface.
Run performance reviews that change the next contract.
Prequalification — Screening a contractor's safety capability before award, on evidence rather than promises.

modules.title: Module 6 — Root-cause investigation: ICAM fundamentals
modules.summary: Level 2 taught five-whys. This module teaches structured causal analysis at organisational level, built on the ICAM (Incident Cause Analysis Method) approach derived from James Reason's organisational-accident model: preconditions, individual actions, task and environmental factors, and organisational factors behind them. The aim is investigations whose recommendations change systems, not memories.
points: Explain the organisational-accident model: latent conditions, active failures, defences.
Structure an ICAM-style investigation: fact gathering, timeline, analysis across the four factor groups.
Distinguish immediate causes from underlying organisational causes in a real incident.
Write findings and recommendations that a board can resource and an auditor can verify.
Recognise the investigation failure modes: stopping at blame, stopping at the first cause, stopping at paperwork.
Latent condition — A system weakness planted in the organisation long before an incident: an unenforced rule, a training gap, a budget choice.

modules.title: Module 7 — Auditing and inspection techniques
modules.summary: This module moves from walking a site to auditing a system: planning an audit programme, building checklists from standards, gathering evidence through documents, interviews and observation, grading findings, and writing reports that get actioned. The same discipline serves internal audits, client audits and preparing to be audited.
points: Distinguish inspection, audit and verification, and schedule each correctly.
Build an audit checklist from a standard or procedure by converting each requirement into an evidence question.
Gather and triangulate evidence: documents, interviews, observation.
Grade findings, major, minor, observation, improvement opportunity, and defend the grading.
Write audit findings that meet the evidence-test and track actions to closure.
Audit — A systematic, documented verification against a standard or requirement.

modules.title: Module 8 — Training of trainers
modules.summary: The programme's final module multiplies it: how to design and deliver safety training that sticks, and how to feed new instructors back into Levels 1 and 2. It covers adult-learning principles, session design, delivery with difficult rooms, and assessment of learning, closing with each learner delivering and receiving feedback on a training segment.
points: Apply adult-learning principles: relevance, experience, practice, respect.
Design a training session from outcomes backward: objectives, activities, checks, timing.
Deliver a training segment managing nerves, questions and difficult participants.
Assess learning with checks tied to the objectives, and give usable feedback.
Describe the path to becoming an Oryx Academy assistant instructor, subject to the credential requirements.
Backward design — Writing objectives first, then assessments, then activities, so everything serves the outcome.

bank.q: Certification to ISO 45001 in Namibia is…
Temporary works must be…
options: Designed/selected by a competent person, checked before first load, inspected on a rhythm

bank.q: Fall-of-ground reporting is treated as the mine's heartbeat because…
options: It is the earliest signal of ground-control drift before a collapse

bank.q: What must every OEL citation carry?
options: Its source, since limits differ by jurisdiction and list

bank.q: The first question of a good investigation is…
options: What made this act reasonable to this person at this moment?

bank.q: A question you cannot answer should be…
options: Owned with a commitment date, then met

modules.title: Safe Work Procedures & Task Analysis
modules.summary: Write, verify and enforce SWPs from task observations: step, hazard, control, competency. The SWP library becomes the operational backbone of the safety officer's mandate.

modules.title: Welfare, Facilities & Housekeeping
modules.summary: Statutory welfare: sanitation, drinking water, change houses, first aid provision. 5S housekeeping as a leading indicator of site discipline.

modules.title: Training Needs & Competency Matrices
modules.summary: Build the competency matrix: legal requirements vs task demands vs demonstrated ability. Schedule statutory refresher windows and verify training effectiveness.

modules.title: H&S Committees & Consultation
modules.summary: Constitute and run the committee: s.43/44 Labour Act roles, meeting discipline, minutes that track actions, and inspection walk-downs with worker representatives.

modules.title: Safety Devices & Maintenance Interface
modules.summary: Guards, interlocks, emergency stops, lifting tackle registers: verify presence and function, manage defeater controls, and coordinate statutory inspection intervals.

modules.title: Incident Recording & Statistics
modules.summary: Maintain the accident register, calculate frequency and severity rates, and present leading/lagging indicators to management review.

modules.title: Emergency Preparedness at Site Level
modules.summary: Site emergency plan: risk-based scenarios, muster and roll-call, extinguisher and spill readiness, drills with evaluation reports and corrective actions.

modules.title: The Safety Officer's Legal Mandate
modules.summary: Appointment letters, statutory duties, inspection powers, enforcement escalation ladder and the ethics of stopping unsafe work.

bank.q: A Safe Work Procedure is verified by…
options: Observing the real task with the crew who perform it
bank.why: SWPs must reflect actual task conditions, verified with the performing crew.

bank.q: The H&S committee under the Labour Act exists to…
options: Enable structured employer-employee consultation on OHS
bank.why: Sections 43-44 create consultation machinery, not a transfer of duty.

bank.q: A competency matrix primarily compares…
options: Legal/task requirements against demonstrated worker ability
bank.why: The matrix exposes gaps between what work demands and what workers can demonstrate.

bank.q: Machine guarding and interlocks are safety devices that must be…
options: Verified present and functional, with defeat governance
bank.why: Presence + function checks and controlled defeat procedures keep devices credible.

bank.q: LTIFR expresses…
options: Lost-time injuries per million hours worked
bank.why: LTIFR = lost-time injuries x 1,000,000 / hours worked.

bank.q: A leading indicator example is…
bank.why: Leading indicators measure preventive activity before harm occurs.

bank.q: After every emergency drill you must…
options: Evaluate performance and close corrective actions
bank.why: Drill evaluation reports drive corrective actions - that is where value is captured.

bank.q: When a production manager orders a guard removed, the safety officer should…
options: Refuse, document, and escalate through the enforcement ladder
bank.why: The statutory mandate requires refusal, documentation and escalation.

academy.title: National Vocational Diploma in OHS Management

modules.title: Enterprise HSE Management Systems
modules.summary: Design the full PDCA system across multi-site operations: policy deployment, roles and authorities, document hierarchies, and integration of quality/environment/safety.

modules.title: Quantitative BowTie & Barrier Management
modules.summary: Move from paper BowTies to barrier health: assign owners, audit frequencies, degradation factors and KPIs per barrier; aggregate residual risk for investment decisions.

modules.title: Internal Audit Programmes
modules.summary: Build the audit universe, annual programme, checklists from legal and standards requirements, nonconformity grading, and audit committee reporting.

modules.title: Multi-Agency Emergency Command
modules.summary: Incident command structures (ICS): roles, unified command with fire services, police and mines rescue; communications plans and resource logistics.

modules.title: Mining & Construction Project Safety
modules.summary: Contractor mobilisation gates, principal-hazards plans, ground control and lifts; the manager's statutory notifications and approvals in mining and construction contexts.

modules.title: Occupational Health Interface
modules.summary: Medical surveillance programmes, fitness-for-work classification, biological monitoring, and managing restrictions and return-to-work plans.

modules.title: Performance Management & Culture
modules.summary: From lagging KPIs to culture maturity models: perception surveys, felt-leadership routines, recognition systems that reinforce genuine reporting.

modules.title: Management Review & Continuous Improvement
modules.summary: The clause-9.3 engine: inputs, outputs, resourcing decisions, and closing the improvement loop with documented executive decisions.

bank.q: Barrier health management assigns each BowTie barrier…
options: An owner, audit frequency and degradation KPIs
bank.why: Barriers become managed assets with ownership and health metrics.

bank.q: An audit nonconformity graded 'major' means…
options: A system failure or absence of a required control
bank.why: Major NCs indicate systemic failure; minors are isolated lapses.

bank.q: Unified command in a multi-agency emergency means…
options: A single command structure with agreed joint objectives across agencies
bank.why: Unified command aligns agencies on shared objectives under one structure.

bank.q: A contractor mobilisation gate verifies…
options: Safety file, medicals, competency, equipment and statutory appointments before site access
bank.why: Gate criteria must be met before any site access.

bank.q: Medical surveillance programmes are selected based on…
options: The health hazards identified in the risk assessment
bank.why: Surveillance targets the actual health hazards assessed on site.

bank.q: Culture maturity is best measured with…
options: Perception surveys plus observation of leadership routines
bank.why: Surveys + observed routines triangulate actual culture state.

bank.q: Management review (clause 9.3) must produce…
options: Documented decisions on improvement and resources
bank.why: The review closes with resourcing and improvement decisions.

bank.q: Statutory mining notifications are triggered by…
options: Defined events (serious injuries, dangerous occurrences) within legal timelines
bank.why: Specific events carry statutory notification deadlines.

academy.title: Diploma in Applied OHS Instrumentation & Hygiene

modules.title: Gas Detection Instrumentation
modules.summary: Catalytic, electrochemical, PID and IR sensor physics; calibration curves, span gas discipline, drift management and cross-sensitivities in field conditions.

modules.title: 4-Gas Field Practicals
modules.summary: Full testing campaigns: stratified sampling plans, pump vs diffusion modes, data logging, and interpretation against action levels (O2, LEL, H2S, CO).

modules.title: Gravimetric Dust Sampling
modules.summary: Respirable and inhalable fractions: cyclone selection, flow calibration, filter handling, mine/quarry sampling plans and lab result interpretation.

modules.title: Noise Measurement & Zoning
modules.summary: Sound level meters, octave bands, dose meters; build plant noise maps, define zones, and specify engineering controls from measurement evidence.

modules.title: WBGT & Heat Stress Management
modules.summary: Wet-bulb globe temperature measurement, acclimatisation schedules, work-rest cycles, hydration protocols and heat illness case management.

modules.title: Radiation Dosimetry (NRPA)
modules.summary: Namibian radiation protection for mining: monitoring programmes, TLD/OSL badges, dose limits, controlled area rules and NRPA licensing interface.

modules.title: Illumination & Ergonomics Survey
modules.summary: Lux surveying for task areas, glare assessment, and ergonomic task analysis integrating anthropometric data for workstation design.

modules.title: Hygiene Report Writing
modules.summary: Convert field data into professional hygiene reports: methodology, limits tables, exceedance findings, prioritised controls and management recommendations.

bank.q: A PID sensor is the correct choice for detecting…
bank.why: Photoionisation detectors respond to volatile organic compounds at ppm concentrations.

bank.q: Bump-testing a gas detector means…
options: Exposing it to calibration gas to verify sensors alarm and respond
bank.why: A bump test confirms sensor response and alarm function before field use.

bank.q: Respirable dust sampling uses a cyclone to…
options: Separate the size fraction that reaches deep lung
bank.why: The cyclone's cut-point selects respirable-size particles for the filter.

bank.q: WBGT integrates…
options: Air temperature, humidity (wet bulb) and radiant heat (globe)
bank.why: WBGT combines wet bulb, dry bulb and globe temperatures for heat stress.

bank.q: The annual whole-body dose limit for radiation workers (Namibia NRPA) is…
bank.why: Occupational effective dose is capped at 20 mSv/year averaged over five years.

bank.q: For an accurate plant noise map, the sound level meter must be…
options: Calibrated before/after with a class-appropriate acoustic calibrator
bank.why: Field calibration before and after each session validates the measurement chain.

bank.q: A hygiene report's control recommendations follow…
options: The hierarchy of controls applied to measured exceedances
bank.why: Exceedances drive control selection through the hierarchy of controls.

bank.q: Diffusion-mode gas detectors differ from pump-mode because they…
options: Rely on ambient air movement to reach the sensors
bank.why: Diffusion units depend on local air movement; pump units draw remote samples via tubing.

academy.title: Advanced Diploma in Strategic EHS, PSM & ESG

modules.title: EIA & EMP Practice (MEFT)
modules.summary: Namibian EIA procedure under the EMA Act: screening, scoping, specialist studies, public participation, environmental clearance and the EMP's binding management actions.

modules.title: Process Safety Management Foundations
modules.summary: PSM pillars: process safety information, HAZOP/LOPA, mechanical integrity, management of change, and process safety KPIs distinct from personal safety metrics.

modules.title: Green Hydrogen Risk Landscape
modules.summary: Hydrogen-specific hazards: wide flammability range, invisible flames, embrittlement; electrolyser safety, storage modes and layer-of-protection design for emerging projects.

modules.title: Occupational Epidemiology
modules.summary: Cohort and case-control thinking applied to workplaces: rates, standardisation, confounders, cluster investigation and ethical use of health data.

modules.title: ISO 45001/14001 Lead Auditing
modules.summary: Lead-audit practice: audit plan construction, process interviewing, objective evidence discipline, reporting and certification-body interfaces (ISO 19011).

modules.title: ESG Integration & Reporting
modules.summary: Link EHS performance to ESG frameworks (GRI, IFRS S2): materiality, social licence, assurance readiness and investor-grade disclosure.

modules.title: Strategic Risk & Board Governance
modules.summary: Present risk to boards: risk appetite statements, assurance maps (three lines model), crisis governance and director-level duties.

modules.title: Capstone: Integrated EHS Strategy
modules.summary: Synthesise the diploma into an executable strategy: maturity baseline, 3-year roadmap, investment case, KPI architecture and executive communication.

bank.q: An EMP's management actions are…
options: Binding commitments audited through the project lifecycle
bank.why: EMP commitments are enforceable conditions tied to environmental clearance.

bank.q: HAZOP identifies deviations by applying…
options: Guidewords to process parameters (e.g., NO FLOW, MORE PRESSURE)
bank.why: HAZOP systematically applies guidewords to design intent deviations.

bank.q: Hydrogen is hazardous partly because its flame…
options: Burns nearly invisibly in daylight with a wide flammability range
bank.why: H2 flames are near-invisible and its 4-75% flammability range is wide.

bank.q: Management of Change (MOC) is triggered by…
options: Any technical, organisational or personnel change affecting process safety
bank.why: MOC covers technical, organisational and staffing changes with safety impact.

bank.q: In epidemiology, a confounder is…
options: A third factor that distorts the apparent exposure-disease relationship
bank.why: Confounders create spurious associations if unaccounted for.

bank.q: ISO 19011 governs…
bank.why: ISO 19011 provides the auditing guideline framework for management systems.

bank.q: The three lines model separates…
options: Operational management, risk/compliance functions, and internal audit
bank.why: First line runs controls, second line oversees, third line assures independently.

bank.q: A board-level risk appetite statement defines…
options: The risk the organisation is willing to accept in pursuit of objectives
bank.why: It calibrates how much risk the board authorises management to carry.

modules.title: The OHS Management System Architecture
modules.summary: Plan-Do-Check-Act applied to ISO 45001:2018: context of the organisation, worker participation, documented information, and the legal register as the system's foundation.

modules.title: ISO 31000 Risk & BowTie Barrier Thinking
modules.summary: Risk assessment methodology from context to treatment. BowTie diagrams make threats, top events, consequences and preventive/recovery barriers explicit and auditable.

modules.title: Contractor & e-PTW Governance
modules.summary: Managing contractor safety from pre-qualification to demobilisation: safety file review, mutual responsibility matrices, and electronic permit-to-work workflows.

modules.title: ISO 14001 Environmental Control & Auditing
modules.summary: Environmental aspects/impacts registers, waste hierarchy, emergency preparedness for spills, and internal audit programmes aligned to ISO 45001 and ISO 14001 clause 9.

bank.q: Under ISO 45001:2018, which clause requires an organisation to determine relevant interested parties and their needs?
bank.why: Clause 4.2 requires understanding the needs and expectations of workers and other interested parties.

bank.q: In a BowTie diagram, the central 'top event' represents…
options: The moment control of the hazard is lost
bank.why: The top event is the loss of control of the hazard; threats sit left, consequences right.

bank.q: A barrier that limits the consequence AFTER the top event has occurred is called a…
bank.why: Recovery barriers act on the right side of the BowTie, reducing consequence severity.

bank.q: ISO 31000 defines risk as the 'effect of uncertainty' on…
bank.why: Risk is the effect of uncertainty on objectives - a deliberately broad definition.

bank.q: Before a contractor mobilises to site, the principal contractor must verify…
options: A site-specific safety file and medical fitness
bank.why: Safety file review and medical fitness verification are gate conditions for mobilisation.

bank.q: Which document records how a task could harm the environment and what controls apply?
bank.why: ISO 14001 requires an aspects/impacts register linking activities to environmental impact and controls.

bank.q: The waste hierarchy gives the highest priority to…
bank.why: Avoidance and reduction sit above reuse, recycling, treatment and disposal.

bank.q: An internal audit of the OHS system must be performed by personnel who are…
options: Objective and impartial relative to the activity audited
bank.why: ISO clause 9.2 requires auditors to be objective and impartial; auditors cannot audit their own work.

modules.title: Scene Safety & DRABC
modules.summary: No rescuer becomes a second casualty. Declare scene hazards, apply gloves, then run Danger-Response-Airway-Breathing-Circulation in strict order.

modules.title: CPR 30:2 - Adult & Child
modules.summary: Compressions pump the heart; breaths oxygenate the blood. 30:2 at 100-120 bpm, 5-6 cm depth in adults, one-third chest depth in children, two fingers for infants.
points: Heel of hand, centre of chest

modules.title: AED & Choking
modules.summary: AEDs analyse rhythm and shock ventricular fibrillation - pad placement and clear-and-shock discipline decide survival. Choking: encourage cough, 5 back blows, 5 abdominal thrusts.
points: Pad placement: right upper, left lower
Recovery position for the breathing casualty

bank.q: The correct adult compression-to-breath ratio for one rescuer is…
bank.why: Current guidelines specify 30 compressions to 2 breaths for adult CPR.

bank.q: Adult compression depth should be…
bank.why: At least 5 cm and not more than 6 cm for adult chest compressions.

bank.q: The target compression rate is…
bank.why: 100-120 compressions per minute balances coronary perfusion with refill time.

bank.q: You check for normal breathing for a maximum of…
bank.why: More than 10 seconds delays compressions; less than 5 s is unreliable.

bank.q: During AED rhythm analysis and shock delivery you must…
bank.why: Anyone in contact with the casualty can receive the shock - call 'clear' and visually confirm.

bank.q: First response to a casualty with severe airway obstruction who cannot cough is…
bank.why: Up to 5 back blows, then up to 5 abdominal thrusts, alternating; blind finger sweeps are prohibited.

bank.q: A casualty who is unresponsive but breathing normally is placed…
bank.why: The recovery position protects the airway of a breathing, unresponsive casualty.

bank.q: Scene safety comes…
bank.why: Danger is the first letter of DRABC - never create a second casualty.

practicum.title: CPR & AED Skills Assessment
practicum.pass_rule: Assessor ticks every line - any unticked item fails the drill.
items: Scene safety declared before approach (hazards, bystanders, PPE/gloves)
DRABC primary survey performed in correct order
Response check: shout and shoulder-tap, then shout for help / call emergency number
Airway opened with head-tilt chin-lift; breathing checked 10 seconds max
30 compressions: centre of chest, 5-6 cm depth, 100-120 bpm
2 rescue breaths with visible chest rise, <10 s interruption
5 cycles of 30:2 completed without pausing beyond 10 s
AED switched on, pads placed correct sides, no one touches during analysis/shock
Compression quality: full recoil, correct hand position, rhythm in time with metronome
Casualty placed in recovery position when breathing returns

modules.title: Primary Survey & Catastrophic Bleeding
modules.summary: Life before limb. Run DRABC, then attack catastrophic haemorrhage with direct pressure, wound packing and tourniquets before any other injury is treated.
points: Tourniquet: 5 cm above wound, note the time

modules.title: Burns, Fractures & Shock
modules.summary: Cool burns for 20 minutes with clean water. Splint fractures with the joint above and below. Treat shock early: supine, warm, legs up, nothing by mouth.
points: Shock signs: pale, cold, clammy, fast weak pulse

modules.title: Environmental & Statutory Duties
modules.summary: Snakebite, heat illness, bites and stings follow regional protocols. The employer must provide, and you must control, a statutory first aid box per GN 156 schedules.
points: Snakebite: immobilise, below heart, no cutting

bank.q: A worker severs two fingers on a saw. Your FIRST priority is…
bank.why: Life before limb: catastrophic haemorrhage control precedes everything else.

bank.q: The correct immediate care for a thermal burn is…
options: Cool with clean running water for 20 minutes
bank.why: 20 minutes of clean cool water limits the burn depth; ice causes further tissue injury.

bank.q: When splinting a fractured forearm you must include…
options: The joint above and below the fracture
bank.why: Immobilising the joints above and below prevents movement at the fracture site.

bank.q: Signs of shock include all EXCEPT…
bank.why: Shock produces a fast, weak pulse; a bounding slow pulse suggests the opposite.

bank.q: For a snakebite on the leg you should…
options: Immobilise the limb below heart level
bank.why: Pressure immobilisation below heart level slows venom spread; cutting and tourniquets worsen outcomes.

bank.q: Heat stroke differs from heat exhaustion because it presents with…
bank.why: Hot dry skin and altered consciousness mean the cooling system has failed - a medical emergency.

bank.q: Casualties in shock should be given…
bank.why: Nothing by mouth - possible surgery and aspiration risk.

bank.q: The statutory first aid box register must record…
options: Date, names, nature of injury and treatment
bank.why: GN 156 first aid regulations require usage registers recording date, casualty, injury and treatment.

practicum.title: Trauma & Medical Emergency Drill
practicum.pass_rule: Assessor ticks every line - any unticked item fails the drill.
items: Scene survey completed; gloves and eye protection worn
Catastrophic haemorrhage controlled with direct pressure and firm dressing
Tourniquet applied high and tight with time written on the casualty (only for uncontrollable limb bleeding)
Burn cooled with clean running water for 20 minutes; no creams, ice or blisters popped
Fracture immobilised including the joint above and below; circulation checked before and after splinting
Shock position: casualty supine, legs elevated, kept warm, nothing by mouth
Snakebite limb immobilised below heart level; no cutting, sucking or tourniquet
Heat exhaustion: moved to shade, cooled, sips of water; heat stroke treated as an emergency (EMS)
First aid box inventory checked against GN 156 Schedule contents and shortages reported
Accident register entry completed with date, names, nature of injury and treatment given

modules.title: Fire Triangle & Fire Classes
modules.summary: Fire needs heat, fuel and oxygen; remove one and it dies. Classes A (solids), B (liquids), C (gases), D (metals), F (cooking oils) plus electrical hazards determine extinguisher choice.

modules.title: Extinguisher Selection & PASS
modules.summary: Water and foam for Class A; DCP for B/C/electrical; CO2 for electrical and liquids. PASS: Pull the pin, Aim at the base, Squeeze, Sweep. Stay upwind, keep your exit behind you.
points: Water never on live equipment or oils
PASS with sweep at the base

modules.title: Fire Marshal Command Duties
modules.summary: The marshal commands the evacuation: raise the alarm, sweep rooms, close doors, execute roll-call against registers, and report all-clear or missing persons to the incident controller.
points: Report to emergency services on arrival

bank.q: A petrol fire in a drum is which fire class?
bank.why: Flammable liquids are Class B fires.

bank.q: The correct extinguisher for an energised electrical panel is…
bank.why: CO2 and DCP are non-conductive; water conducts electricity.

bank.q: PASS stands for…
bank.why: Pull the pin, Aim low at the base, Squeeze the handle, Sweep side to side.

bank.q: You aim the extinguisher at…
bank.why: Sweeping the base attacks the fuel surface where combustion occurs.

bank.q: When fighting a small fire you should always keep…
bank.why: Never let fire come between you and your escape route.

bank.q: A fire marshal's roll-call must include…
options: Staff and visitors from the register
bank.why: Visitor and contractor registers are checked so no one is left inside.

bank.q: Removing the fuel source from a fire attacks which side of the fire triangle?
bank.why: Isolating the fuel supply starves the fire.

bank.q: A cooking-oil fire in the canteen fryer is best handled with…
options: Wet chemical extinguisher or fire blanket
bank.why: Wet chemical saponifies burning oil; water causes a violent eruption.

practicum.title: Live Extinguisher & Evacuation Drill
practicum.pass_rule: Assessor ticks every line - any unticked item fails the drill.
items: Fire class correctly identified before extinguisher selection
Correct extinguisher chosen (water/foam/DCP/CO2) and selection justified aloud
PASS technique demonstrated: Pull, Aim low at base, Squeeze, Sweep side to side
Extinguisher discharged from upwind position with escape route kept behind
Standing distance adjusted (1-2 m) as the flame diminishes without approaching smoke
Fire blanket correctly deployed over a pan fire with hands shielded
Hose reel run-out and flow demonstrated without kinking
Assembly point roll-call executed against the visitor and staff register
Sweeps of toilets and isolated rooms performed and reported
Incident report: time, location, class, extinguisher used and actions logged

modules.title: Fall Physics: Factor & Clearance
modules.summary: Fall factor = fall distance / lanyard length. Factor 2 is survivable only with rated anchors and shock absorbers. Clearance must cover lanyard + deceleration + body + margin.

modules.title: Harness & Lanyard Inspection
modules.summary: Inspect before every use: cuts, burns, chemical attack, hardened webbing, deployed tear-away indicators, locked gates, stamped dates and rated markings.

modules.title: 100% Tie-Off & Rescue
modules.summary: Twin-hook lanyards keep you attached at every step. Above all: a rescue plan. Suspension trauma can kill a conscious worker in 15 minutes - rotate legs, rescue fast.

bank.q: A fall factor of 2 occurs when…
options: The worker never leaves the platform
The fall distance is twice the lanyard length
The anchor is at foot level with a full lanyard fall
bank.why: Foot-level anchoring with a 2 m lanyard allows a 4 m free fall - factor 2, the worst case.

bank.q: The dorsal (rear) D-ring of a full-body harness is used for…
bank.why: The centre-back D-ring is the primary fall-arrest attachment point.

bank.q: A deployed tear-away indicator on a shock absorber means…
options: The unit has arrested a fall and must be removed from service
bank.why: Any deployed absorber or post-fall hardware must be destroyed, never reused.

bank.q: Fall clearance calculation must include…
options: Lanyard + deceleration distance + worker height + safety margin
bank.why: All four elements prevent striking the ground or obstruction below.

bank.q: During 100% tie-off on a ladder or beam, the rule is…
options: Both hooks may be open briefly
At least one hook is always attached
Tie off only at the top
bank.why: Continuous attachment: one hook always connected during transitions.

bank.q: Suspension trauma after an arrested fall is managed by…
options: Leaving the casualty hanging until they feel better
Prompt rescue within minutes and semi-sitting positioning
bank.why: Prompt rescue and careful positioning prevent pooled blood shock on release.

bank.q: A scaffold may be used only when it carries…
options: A green inspection tag, current and signed
bank.why: Green means inspected and safe; red or missing tags prohibit access.

bank.q: Anchor points for fall arrest must be rated at least…
options: 10 kN per person (or 15 kN non-certified structures)
bank.why: Certified anchors: 10 kN per attached person; non-certified structures: 15 kN with supervision.

practicum.title: Harness Donning & Tie-Off Assessment
practicum.pass_rule: Assessor ticks every line - any unticked item fails the drill.
items: Pre-use inspection of harness: webbing, stitching, buckles, D-ring, tags (no cuts, burns, chemical damage)
Fall-arrest lanyard inspected: tear-away indicators intact, snaphook gates lock
Harness donned fully with all five adjustment points snug (legs, waist, chest, shoulders)
D-ring located between shoulder blades; buddy check completed aloud
Anchor point verified: rated, above the worker, in line with the swing fall path
Twin lanyards used in 100% tie-off - never both hooks detached
Calculates fall clearance: lanyard length + deceleration distance + body height + safety margin
Work position adjusted so free-fall distance stays under 2 m and fall factor stays at or below 1
Rescue plan stated aloud: who raises the alarm, retrieval method, suspension trauma relief
Post-fall protocol: casualty rescued within 15 minutes and kept in a semi-sitting rescue position

modules.title: Confined Spaces & Atmospheric Hazards
modules.summary: A confined space is defined by access, not size. Gases stratify: methane rises to the top, oxygen is displaced mid-space, H2S and CO sink low. Test every level, every time.
points: Definition: restricted entry, not designed for occupancy
Gas densities: CH4 < air < O2 > H2S/CO
H2S 10 ppm / CO 25 ppm action levels

modules.title: 4-Gas Detector Discipline
modules.summary: Zero in clean air, bump against calibration gas, then test top-middle-bottom. If the instrument fails or alarms - no entry, no exceptions, no overrides.
points: Zero vs bump vs full calibration
Never trust smell - H2S numbs the nose

modules.title: Permits, Standby & Non-Entry Rescue
modules.summary: Entry needs a permit with test results, ventilation, isolation, communications and rescue rigged. The attendant never enters; the tripod does.

bank.q: The acceptable oxygen band for confined-space entry is…
options: Any, if the LEL is low
bank.why: Below 19.5% is oxygen-deficient; above 23.5% is oxygen-enriched and fire-prone.

bank.q: In a stratified atmosphere, H2S will be found…
bank.why: H2S is heavier than air and pools at the lowest point.

bank.q: Before every shift's gas testing the detector must be…
options: Zeroed in clean air and bump-tested against calibration gas
bank.why: Zero + bump confirms the sensors respond correctly before trusting readings.

bank.q: The correct stratification test order from top to bottom is…
bank.why: LEL (methane) sits high, O2 mid, H2S/CO low - test in that vertical order at each depth.

bank.q: The standby attendant's primary rule is…
options: Enter immediately if the entrant collapses
Leave the log unattended for breaks
bank.why: Untrained rescuers die most often; the attendant maintains watch and summons the rescue team.

bank.q: For hot work inside a confined space the LEL must read…
bank.why: Hot work requires 0% LEL - any flammable concentration is unacceptable with an ignition source.

bank.q: H2S is particularly dangerous because at high concentrations it…
options: Paralyzes the sense of smell and causes rapid collapse
bank.why: Olfactory fatigue means 'no smell' never means 'no gas'.

bank.q: Non-entry rescue primarily relies on…
options: Tripod, winch and entrant's retrieval harness
bank.why: Rigged retrieval equipment recovers the entrant without exposing rescuers.

practicum.title: Gas Test & Entry Drill
practicum.pass_rule: Assessor ticks every line - any unticked item fails the drill.
items: Detector zeroed in clean air and bump-test verified against calibration gas before testing
Stratification sequence followed: top (methane/LEL), middle (O2), bottom (H2S/CO) at every level reached
O2 reading confirmed 19.5-23.5% before any further testing
LEL below 5% (0% for hot work) confirmed and recorded
H2S below 10 ppm and CO below 25 ppm confirmed and recorded
Results written on the entry permit with time, depth and instrument serial
Ventilation established and re-test after any break in work
Entrant wears harness with retrieval line; standby attendant holds the log and keeps continuous communication
Attendant never enters; tripod and winch rigged for non-entry retrieval before entry
Permit closed out: space vacated, seals replaced, register signed

modules.title: The Six-Step Isolation Sequence
modules.summary: Identify all energies, notify, shut down, isolate, lock and tag, then verify with Try-Out. Stored energy kills after the switch is already open - bleed, block, pin, restrain.
points: Lock + tag at EVERY isolation point
Verify by Try-Out, never by trust

modules.title: Locks, Hasps & Tags
modules.summary: One worker, one lock, one key. Group isolation uses a hasp so every worker adds a personal lock. Tags inform - locks protect. Only the owner removes their lock.

modules.title: Zero-Energy Try-Out
modules.summary: Verification closes the loop: press start, watch for movement, read the gauges, test electrically dead. No Try-Out, no work - every time, every task.

bank.q: The mandatory final step before working on isolated equipment is…
bank.why: Verification proves zero energy: attempt start, check gauges, test dead.

bank.q: In group isolation, each worker must…
options: Attach a personal lock to a multi-lock hasp
bank.why: A hasp allows multiple personal locks - everyone protects themselves.

bank.q: A danger tag by itself…
options: Only warns - only a lock prevents operation
Can be reused for the next job
bank.why: Tags inform; locks physically prevent energisation.

bank.q: Which energy form is most often forgotten during isolation?
bank.why: Capacitors, accumulators, raised loads and springs store lethal energy after shut-down.

bank.q: Locks are removed after the job by…
options: The lock owner only (with a documented exception procedure)
The shift supervisor at any time
The safety officer with bolt cutters
bank.why: Only the owner removes their lock; exception procedures exist with formal verification.

bank.q: Residual pneumatic pressure is released by…
options: Bleeding the line to zero and verifying on gauges
bank.why: Bleed-down and gauge verification achieve true zero pressure.

bank.q: Before electrical work an electrician must…
options: Test the circuit is dead with a proven meter
bank.why: Test-before-touch with a meter proven on a known live source.

bank.q: If the job runs past the shift, the lock…
options: Stays, and the incoming worker applies their own lock before the old one is removed
Is swapped for a zip tie
bank.why: Lock exchange follows the documented procedure: new lock applied before old lock removed.

practicum.title: Isolation & Try-Out Drill
practicum.pass_rule: Assessor ticks every line - any unticked item fails the drill.
items: All energy sources identified on the isolation certificate (electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic, mechanical, gravitational, thermal, stored/residual)
Machine notified and shut down by normal operating procedure
Electrical isolator locked open with a personal padlock, one worker one lock one key
Pneumatic/hydraulic residual pressure bled to zero and verified on gauges
Raised loads blocked or pinned; springs restrained; gravity neutralised
Danger tag completed: name, date, department, reason - legible and attached at every isolation point
Multi-worker job uses a lock hasp so each worker applies a personal lock
Try-Out performed: attempt start controls, check gauges read zero, verify no movement, test with meter where applicable
Locks removed ONLY by their owners after work completion sign-off
Isolation register closed and equipment returned to service with operational check

modules.title: HIRA Types & the 5x5 Matrix
modules.summary: Baseline HIRA maps the operation; issue-based HIRA answers change and incidents; continuous HIRA lives in the DSTI. Score consequence x likelihood on the 5x5 matrix and act on the band.

modules.title: Hierarchy of Controls
modules.summary: Eliminate, substitute, engineer, administrate, then PPE. PPE protects one person only after every other layer has failed - never the first answer.
points: Elimination is the only true fix
Engineering controls don't rely on behaviour
PPE = last line, first to fail

modules.title: DSTI Facilitation & Section 42
modules.summary: The DSTI converts today's HIRA into a 5-minute crew briefing: tasks, hazards, controls, emergency actions. Section 42 of the Labour Act protects any worker who refuses unsafe work in good faith.

bank.q: On a 5x5 matrix, a risk scoring 20 falls in the band requiring…
bank.why: 16-25 is intolerable: stop the task until risk is reduced.

bank.q: The FIRST level of the hierarchy of controls is…
bank.why: Eliminating the hazard removes the risk entirely - everything else manages it.

bank.q: A continuous HIRA is best delivered as…
options: The Daily Safe Task Instruction briefing
bank.why: The DSTI carries today's hazards to today's crew before work starts.

bank.q: Section 42 of the Namibian Labour Act protects workers who…
options: Refuse unsafe work in good faith
bank.why: Good-faith refusal of unsafe work is a protected right - no victimisation.

bank.q: Risk is scored by multiplying…
bank.why: The 5x5 matrix multiplies worst credible consequence by likelihood.

bank.q: An issue-based HIRA is triggered by…
options: New equipment, process changes, or after incidents
bank.why: Change and incident learnings demand a fresh issue-based assessment.

bank.q: PPE is ranked LAST in the hierarchy because…
options: It protects only the wearer and fails with human behaviour
bank.why: PPE's protection collapses when fit, discipline or maintenance fail.

bank.q: A DSTI briefing must include…
options: Tasks, hazards, controls and emergency actions
bank.why: The DSTI structure keeps the briefing on hazards and controls.

modules.title: Silica: The Invisible Killer
modules.summary: Respirable crystalline silica (particles under 4 microns) scars the lung permanently - silicosis, COPD, lung cancer. You cannot see the dust that kills; visibility is a warning, not a measure.
points: Silicosis, COPD, lung cancer, TB link
High-risk tasks: cutting, drilling, crushing, sanding

modules.title: Measurement & Engineering Controls
modules.summary: Gravimetric pumps sample at defined flow rates onto filters for lab analysis. Engineering controls come first: wet methods, on-tool extraction, enclosure.

modules.title: RPE Programme Discipline
modules.summary: Respirators are the last line: fit-testing, shave-to-seal, filter change schedules, and clean-shaven policy where tight-fitting masks are used.

bank.q: The respirable fraction that reaches deep lung tissue is smaller than…
bank.why: Particles under about 4 microns penetrate to the gas-exchange region.

bank.q: Diseases caused by crystalline silica include…
bank.why: Silicosis, COPD, lung cancer and TB are the established silica outcomes.

bank.q: The preferred control for a concrete-cutting task is…
bank.why: Wet methods and LEV control at source, above any PPE.

bank.q: A tight-fitting respirator will NOT seal correctly if the wearer…
bank.why: Any facial hair at the seal line leaks - fit-test with the actual wearer and shaving policy.

bank.q: Visible dust in the air means…
options: The air is safe between puffs
Exposure is far above limits - the respirable fraction is invisible
bank.why: If you can SEE dust, respirable exposure is already severe.

bank.q: Gravimetric dust sampling measures…
options: Mass of dust collected on a filter over time
bank.why: A calibrated pump draws air through a filter; lab weighing gives mg/m3.

modules.title: The dBA Scale & 85 dBA Action Level
modules.summary: Decibels are logarithmic: +3 dBA doubles the energy, +10 dBA sounds twice as loud. At 85 dBA over 8 hours hearing damage begins - the action level for a hearing conservation programme.
points: Halving rule: every +3 dBA halves safe time
85 dBA: you must raise your voice at 1 m

modules.title: Noise Mapping & Controls
modules.summary: Map the plant with a sound level meter; zone red areas; fix the source first - silencers, damping, isolation, enclosures - before hearing protection is prescribed.

modules.title: Hearing Protection & Audiometry
modules.summary: Muffs and plugs only work when worn every second in the zone. Fit, NRR derating, dual protection above 100 dBA, and baseline audiograms detect damage early.

bank.q: An 8-hour exposure limit triggering a conservation programme is…
bank.why: 85 dBA over 8 hours is the standard action level.

bank.q: An increase from 85 dBA to 91 dBA…
options: Doubles sound energy twice - safe exposure time drops from 8 h to 2 h
bank.why: +3 dBA doubles energy; +6 dBA = 4x, cutting safe time by a factor of 4.

bank.q: The most effective noise control is…
bank.why: Source control (silencers, damping, enclosures) beats protection issued to receivers.

bank.q: You must raise your voice to talk to someone 1 m away when noise exceeds about…
bank.why: Voice-raising at 1 m is the field indicator of ~85 dBA.

bank.q: A 30 dB NRR plug worn correctly provides roughly…
bank.why: Real-world derating halves nominal ratings; lab numbers overstate protection.

bank.q: Audiometric testing detects…
options: Early hearing threshold shifts before workers notice
bank.why: Baseline and periodic audiograms catch standard threshold shifts early.

modules.title: Permit Types & Systems
modules.summary: A permit is a formal hand-over of a controlled hazard envelope: hot work, cold work, vessel entry, excavation, electrical. One permit, one task, one place, one validity.

modules.title: Authorised vs Performing Authority
modules.summary: The Authorised Person (AP) isolates, tests and issues; the Performing Authority (PA) executes; both sign handover and hand-back. Nobody signs for someone else.

modules.title: Permit Content & Close-Out
modules.summary: A valid permit states the exact task, location, isolation points, gas results with times, PPE, emergency plan - and is suspended for any change. Close-out returns the plant to operations formally.

bank.q: A permit-to-work transfers…
options: Responsibility for a controlled hazard envelope from issuer to acceptor
bank.why: The signed handover formally transfers control of the hazard for a defined task.

bank.q: One permit covers…
options: The whole plant for a week
One task, one place, one validity period
bank.why: Scope discipline: one task, one location, one time window.

bank.q: The Performing Authority may…
options: Execute the task only after accepting the permit conditions
Sign on behalf of the AP
bank.why: The PA accepts conditions before work; neither party signs for the other.

bank.q: A permit must be suspended when…
options: Any condition changes - weather, scope, personnel, plant state
bank.why: Changed conditions invalidate the risk envelope - suspend, reassess, reissue.

bank.q: Gas test results on a confined space permit must include…
options: Reading, time and tester identity at each level
bank.why: Recorded values, times and tester make the results auditable.

bank.q: Close-out of a permit means…
options: Formal hand-back: work complete, isolations restored, register signed
bank.why: Hand-back returns the plant to operations with the register closed.

modules.title: Reporting Culture & First Response
modules.summary: Every near miss is free tuition. First response: make safe, care for people, preserve the scene, notify per statutory timelines. Blame kills reporting - just culture is the foundation.

modules.title: The ICAM Framework
modules.summary: ICAM analyses five tiers: environmental/personnel factors, front-line acts, task factors, organisational factors. It asks 'why did this make sense at the time?' - not 'who do we fire?'

modules.title: Corrective Actions That Stick
modules.summary: Actions target systems, not symptoms: engineering and process changes rank above 'retrain and remind'. Track owners, due dates, verification of effectiveness, and close only on evidence.

bank.q: ICAM's core question is…
options: Why did the actions of reasonable people make sense at the time?
How much will the claim cost?
bank.why: ICAM is a systems analysis, not a blame hunt.

bank.q: The first actions at an incident scene are…
options: Make safe, care for casualties, preserve the scene, notify
bank.why: Life, scene preservation and statutory notification come before analysis.

bank.q: In ICAM, the most powerful findings usually sit in…
options: Organisational factors - planning, resourcing, supervision design
bank.why: Organisational factors shape the conditions front-line acts emerge from.

bank.q: A strong corrective action is…
options: An engineering change or process redesign with an owner and due date
bank.why: System fixes with ownership and verification actually prevent recurrence.

bank.q: Near misses are valuable because…
options: They are free lessons about failed barriers before someone is hurt
bank.why: The near-miss pyramid shows many precursors under each serious injury.

bank.q: A corrective action may be closed when…
options: Evidence shows the fix is implemented and effective
bank.why: Closure requires verification of implementation AND effectiveness.

modules.title: Aspects, Impacts & ISO 14001
modules.summary: An aspect is how your activity touches the environment; the impact is the change it causes. Rate significance, then control: the aspects register drives operational controls and objectives.

modules.title: Waste Streams & the 4Rs
modules.summary: Reduce, reuse, recycle, recover - then dispose. Segregate at source: general, recyclable, hazardous, scrap. Hazardous waste moves only with manifests and approved contractors.

modules.title: Spills, Bunding & EMA Duty of Care
modules.summary: Secondary containment (bunding) holds 110% of the largest vessel. Spill kits, boom placement and drain covers stop escapes. The EMA Act imposes a general duty of care - polluters remediate.

bank.q: In ISO 14001, an 'aspect' is…
options: The element of an activity that interacts with the environment
bank.why: Aspect = the interaction (e.g., diesel storage); impact = the change (e.g., soil contamination).

bank.q: The waste hierarchy's first preference is…
bank.why: Reduce, then reuse, recycle, recover - disposal is last.

bank.q: Bunding for a fuel tank should hold at least…
options: Nothing if the ground is flat
bank.why: Secondary containment of 110% captures catastrophic failure plus rain.

bank.q: Hazardous waste may leave site only…
options: With a completed manifest to an approved contractor
bank.why: The manifest chain proves cradle-to-grave control.

bank.q: During a diesel spill near a storm drain you first…
options: Deploy drain covers/booms, then contain and absorb
bank.why: Stop the escape path first - drains lead directly to watercourses.

bank.q: Namibia's EMA Act imposes…
options: A general duty of care with remediation liability on polluters
bank.why: The Environmental Management Act creates duty-of-care and remediation obligations.
